paraphrase: DLMF 18.14.25 states that sum_{m=0}^{n} [(lam+1)_{n-m}/(n-m)!] [(lam+1)_m/m!] P_m^{(al,be)}(x)/P_m^{(be,al)}(1) >= 0 for x >= -1, al+be >= lam >= 0, be >= -1/2 and EVERY n = 0,1,...; 18.14.26 is the Askey-Gasper inequality, the lam = 0 case, valid under al+be >= 0, be >= -1/2 or al+be >= -2, be >= 0. The DLMF annotations credit the proofs to Gasper (1977, Theorems 5 and 4) and the conjectures to Askey-Gasper (1976). This is the canonical example of a positivity statement that is UNIFORM in the degree index.
limitations: The uniform index here is the DEGREE n of a sum of polynomials evaluated at a point x; our keystone needs uniformity in the trajectory/depth index of a COEFFICIENT. Different object; a bridge is required, not a citation.
Verified through the DLMF page only; the underlying Gasper 1977 and Askey-Gasper 1976 papers were not obtained.

source.title: Gasper, Positive Sums of the Classical Orthogonal Polynomials, SIAM J. Math. Anal. 8 (1977) 423-447

location.section: publisher abstract; Theorems 4 and 5 per DLMF annotations

paraphrase: The published abstract states the METHOD, not just the result: 'An expansion as a sum of squares of Jacobi polynomials P_n^{(al,be)}(x) is used to prove that if 0 <= lam <= al+be and be >= -1/2 then (*) >= 0, -1 <= x < infinity', with equality only at x = -1 for odd n and at lam = 0, al = -be = 1/2. So a single explicit sum-of-squares identity discharges an infinite family of inequalities indexed by n.
limitations: ABSTRACT ONLY: the SOS identity itself was not read, so I cannot say whether an analogue exists for coefficient positivity.
Paywalled (SIAM). Cannot check whether the SOS construction is index-uniform by accident or by design.

source.title: Szwarc, Connection Coefficients of Orthogonal Polynomials, Canad. Math. Bull. 35 (1992) 548-556

paraphrase: Gives sufficient conditions under which ALL coefficients in the expansion of P_n in terms of Q_0,...,Q_n are non-negative, for two families orthogonal with respect to different measures. The companion SIAM papers (doi:10.1137/0523052, 10.1137/0523053) obtain nonnegative linearization of any product P_n P_m by a discrete boundary-value / maximum-principle argument on the two-index recursion, i.e. one argument covering all index pairs at once.
limitations: ABSTRACT ONLY: the actual sufficient conditions are not read, so applicability to our q (a single polynomial with roots in arithmetic progression, not a member of an orthogonal family) is UNTESTED.

The project's closed-route list already rejects 'a recursion in the knife index' as non-hypergeometric; Szwarc's method does not need a hypergeometric form, but that distinction is my inference, not a verified reading.

source.title: Pillwein, Positivity of certain sums over Jacobi kernel polynomials, Adv. Appl. Math. 41 (2008) 365-377

paraphrase: A computer-assisted proof of positivity of sums over kernel polynomials for ultraspherical Jacobi polynomials. Establishes that machine-produced certificates (holonomic closure plus cylindrical algebraic decomposition, in the Gerhold-Kauers style) are an accepted route to positivity results that hold for every value of a discrete index.
limitations: ABSTRACT ONLY (one sentence). The certificate format, the induction scheme, and whether the argument is uniform in more than one index are all unknown.
Elsevier paywall.

source.title: Kauers & Pillwein, When can we detect that a P-finite sequence is positive?, ISSAC 2010, 195-201

paraphrase: Two algorithms prove positivity of sequences satisfying linear recurrences with polynomial coefficients (P-finite). They succeed on many examples but are NOT guaranteed to terminate, and do not terminate for every input; a priori termination criteria are supplied only for restricted classes of recurrences of order at most three.
limitations: ABSTRACT ONLY.
This is the honest ceiling on the computer-algebra route: there is no general decision procedure, so 'run the CAD prover on the depth-d family' is not automatically a keystone.

source.title: Gneiting, Strictly and non-strictly positive definite functions on spheres, Bernoulli 19(4) 2013

paraphrase: Theorem 1(a) restates Schoenberg (1942): the class Psi_d of isotropic positive definite functions on S^d is EXACTLY the set of functions whose Gegenbauer expansion in C_n^{(d-1)/2} has nonnegative coefficients. Theorem 2(b),(c): Psi_{d+1} is contained in Psi_d, strictly. Section 4.3: completely monotone functions lie in Psi_d for every d.
limitations: PRIOR-ART WARNING for the project: the descent step used in lab/keystone_dimension_walk.py ('positivity at D+2 implies positivity at D, uniformly in spin') is the classical dimension walk Psi_{d+1} subset Psi_d. It must be cited, not presented as new.

Confirms the project's own verdict (OPEN_PROBLEM.md closed route 17): Schoenberg is a restatement of the problem, and the usable sufficient conditions in this literature (monotonicity, convexity, complete monotonicity) are all violated by q, which oscillates by construction.

source.title: Simmons-Duffin, A Semidefinite Program Solver for the Conformal Bootstrap, JHEP 06 (2015) 174

location.section: Sec. 2.1 (polynomial matrix programs); Sec. 3.2 numbered item 1; Appendix A

paraphrase: The bootstrap SDP machinery certifies positivity exactly and uniformly in the CONTINUOUS variable Delta (a Positivstellensatz on the half line, encoded as a polynomial matrix program). Spin is NOT certified: Sec. 3.2 item 1 says verbatim that the infinitely many spin conditions are handled by including spins only up to a finite lmax and that positivity for l > lmax 'should' hold; Appendix A says it is verified post hoc on spins that were not included.
limitations: This is the standard tool paper, not an exhaustive survey; a rigorous large-spin argument may exist elsewhere (SDPB cites ref. [27] = arXiv:1406.7845 for 'a more careful analysis', which I have not read).
Conformal bootstrap, not S-matrix bootstrap; the S-matrix side may differ.

source.title: Mansfield, Positivity of the Veneziano Amplitude in Ten Dimensions

paraphrase: Proves B^D_{n,j} >= 0 for ALL n and ALL j for the type-I Veneziano amplitude in D <= 10, directly from the beta function, with no appeal to the no-ghost theorem. Mechanism: the AEHM double-contour representation (2.11) makes the coefficient the (x^{-1}y^{-1}) residue of a product of two Laurent series; in D <= 6 both series have only nonnegative coefficients so positivity is manifest; at D = 10 the finitely many negative Laurent coefficients are cancelled by adding a rational function P_j(x,y) of vanishing residue (2.14)-(2.15), and the remaining infinite set Q^j_{mu,nu} is shown nonnegative by INDUCTION ON j through the convolution recursion (2.20) with Gregory coefficients, plus a finite list of lemmas and a finite base case. Sec. 3.1 upgrades this to the closed string: the type-II Virasoro-Shapiro residue is the SQUARE of the Veneziano residue, and a product of two positive Gegenbauer combinations is again positive because j (x) j' of SO(D-1) decomposes into a positive sum of irreps. Sec. 3.2 proves B^5_{n,j} >= 0 for all n, j for the massless hypergeometric amplitude, which the paper states arises in the lambda -> 0 limit of the Cheung-Hillman-Remmen planar analogue amplitude (their ref. [25] = arXiv:2408.03362).
limitations: Undeformed spacing only: their residue is a rising factorial with unit spacing, ours is the CHR lambda-deformation with root spacing 2/s. The Gregory-coefficient expansion (2.18) is specific to z/log(1-z) and has no verified lambda-deformed counterpart.
Their induction is in j at fixed generating function; our depth d changes the polynomial itself. The bridge is unproved.
The D <= 10 step requires a paper-specific finite hand computation (eight negative Laurent coefficients); nothing guarantees the analogous finite set stays finite as lambda varies.
Sec. 3.2 covers only D = 5 and only the lambda -> 0 endpoint of our family, so it does NOT settle our problem.

source.title: Arkani-Hamed, Eberhardt, Huang, Mizera, On Unitarity of Tree-Level String Amplitudes, JHEP 02 (2022) 197

paraphrase: Sec. 4.1: the double-contour formula (4.2) makes unitarity MANIFEST for D <= 6 because the integrand factorises into three power series each with only non-negative Taylor coefficients: 1/((1-x)(-log(1-x))^{(D-2)/2}), which is positive exactly for D <= 6 (Eq. 4.3); (x-y)^{-(n-j)} (Eq. 4.4); and the last factor, via positivity of f(z) = 1/log(1-x) + 1/x (Eqs. 4.5-4.6). One argument, all n, all j. Sec. 3: KLT gives Res_{s=n} A_{a,b} = (Res_{s=n} A_a)(Res_{s=n} A_b) (3.22), so closed-string positivity follows from the open-string case. Sec. 4.3.1: fixed j, large n asymptotics via deformation to a HANKEL CONTOUR and x = 1 + t/n, yielding beta^D_{n,j} ~ n^{j+(D-4)/2}/((j+(D-4)/2)! log(n)^{(D-2)/2}) > 0 (4.16), with a full asymptotic series in 1/log(n). Sec. 4.3.2: fixed Delta = n - j (one Regge trajectory), large n, by a saddle point at u = -2.
limitations: NEGATIVE ON THE MOST-WANTED ITEM: neither asymptotic derivation carries explicit error bounds. Eq. (4.14)->(4.15) is justified only by 'the remaining integrand converges uniformly for any bounded domain of the t-plane and hence we can replace it with its value at large n'; Sec. 4.3.2 by 'we can replace u with -2 in most places'. So this section does NOT give a rigorous threshold in n, which is exactly what OPEN_PROBLEM.md asks for.

PRIOR-ART MATCH: the Hankel-contour reduction with the 1/log(n) structure in (4.13)-(4.14) is the same mechanism as the project's 'live route' one-dimensional Hankel integral with exp[-tau/(L - log t)], L = log N. Must be cited.
Undeformed spacing only (Veneziano/Virasoro-Shapiro); no lam-deformed analogue of the positive functions in Appendix A is verified.
Appendix A ('Some positive functions', p.25) and Appendix C (derivations, p.30) were NOT read.

source.title: Cheung, Hillman, Remmen (CHR), appendix closed forms for the partial wave coefficients

paraphrase: Eq. (A3) gives the general partial wave coefficient a_{n,l} of the family as an explicit double sum; Eq. (A4) gives a CLOSED FORM for the leading Regge trajectory l = n and Eq. (A5) a closed form for the FIRST SUBLEADING trajectory l = n-1, expressed as a manifestly explicit multiple of a_{n,n}. No closed form or positivity statement is given beyond the first subleading trajectory.
limitations: Read only at the appendix equations located by grep in the extracted text; the surrounding derivation was not re-read in this pass.
Metadata for this paper comes from the pre-existing project record EV-QG-0004 and was not independently re-verified today.

source.title: Semantic Scholar citation scan of arXiv:2406.02665 and arXiv:2408.03362

paraphrase: Combined citation lists of the two CHR papers: 33 and 25 citing works, 35 distinct after deduplication. A regular-expression scan of every returned title and abstract for phrases such as 'all partial waves', 'all spins', 'every spin', 'positivity of all', 'uniform in spin' returned ZERO hits. On that evidence, no work citing the CHR papers announces positivity of all trajectories of the CHR graviton family.
limitations: SEARCH RESULT, NOT PRIMARY EVIDENCE. Only titles and abstracts were scanned; a result could be buried in a section of a paper whose abstract advertises something else.
Full text was read for only 7 of the 35 citing works.
Semantic Scholar citation coverage is incomplete, especially for 2026 preprints; a paper not citing CHR would be missed entirely.
